children.text: atha vakṣye mantrakośaṃ yad uktaṃ bhūtaḍāmare /
children.translated_text: Now I shall speak the treasury of <s>mantras</s> as taught in the <s>Bhūtaḍāmara</s>,
The sequential arrangement of <s>bījas</s> (seed syllables), arising from the knowledge of the meaning of revealed texts. (verse 1)
The blessed <s>Śiva</s> spoke:

children.text: a vidyujjihvā ā kālavajrī i garjinī ī dhūmrabhairavī u kālarātriḥ ū vidārī ṛ mahāraudrī ṝ bhayaṃkarī ḷ saṃhāriṇī lu karālinī e ūrdhvakeśī ai ugrabhairavī o bhīmākṣī au ḍākinī aṃ rudrarākiṇī aḥ caṇḍikā ka krodhīśaḥ kha vāmanaḥ ga caṇḍaḥ gha vikārī ṅa unmattabhairavaḥ ca jvālāmukhaḥ cha raktadaṃṣṭraḥ ja asitāṅgaḥ jha vaḍavāmukhaḥ ja vidyunmukhaḥ ṭa mahājvālaḥ ṭha kapālī ḍa bhīṣaṇaḥ ḍha ruruḥ ṇa saṃhārī ta bhairavaḥ tha daṇḍī da balibhuk dha ugrasūladhṛk na siṃhanādī pa kapardī pha karālāgniḥ ba bhayaṃkaraḥ bha bahurūpī ma mahākālaḥ ya jīvātmā ra kṣatajokṣitaḥ la balabhedī va raktapaṭaḥ śa caṇḍīśaḥ ṣa jvalanadhvajaḥ sa dhūmadhvajaḥ ha vyomavaktraḥ kṣa tryailokyagrasanātmakaḥ // 2
children.translated_text: a [is] <s>Vidyujjihvā</s> (Lightning-tongued); ā [is] <s>Kālavajrī</s>; i [is] <s>Garjinī</s> (Thundering); ī [is] <s>Dhūmrabhairavī</s> (Smoky-fierce); u [is] <s>Kālarātrī</s> (Dark Night); ū [is] <s>Vidārī</s>; ṛ [is] <s>Mahāraudrī</s> (Great Terrible); ṝ [is] <s>Bhayaṃkarī</s> (Fear-causing); ḷ [is] <s>Saṃhāriṇī</s> (Destroyer); lu [is] <s>Karālinī</s> (Gaping); e [is] <s>Ūrdhvakeśī</s> (Upward-haired); ai [is] <s>Ugrabhairavī</s> (Fierce-terrible); o [is] <s>Bhīmākṣī</s> (Terrible-eyed); au [is] <s>Ḍākinī</s>; aṃ [is] <s>Rudrarākiṇī</s>; aḥ [is] <s>Caṇḍikā</s>; ka [is] <s>Krodhīśa</s> (Lord of Wrath); kha [is] <s>Vāmana</s> (Dwarf); ga [is] <s>Caṇḍa</s> (Fierce); gha [is] <s>Vikārī</s> (Transformer); ṅa [is] <s>Unmattabhairava</s> (Mad Bhairava); ca [is] <s>Jvālāmukha</s> (Flame-faced); cha [is] <s>Raktadaṃṣṭra</s> (Blood-fanged); ja [is] <s>Asitāṅga</s> (Dark-limbed); jha [is] <s>Vaḍavāmukha</s> (Mare-fire-faced); ja [is] <s>Vidyunmukha</s> (Lightning-faced); ṭa [is] <s>Mahājvāla</s> (Great Flame); ṭha [is] <s>Kapālī</s> (Skull-bearer); ḍa [is] <s>Bhīṣaṇa</s> (Terrifying); ḍha [is] <s>Ruru</s>; ṇa [is] <s>Saṃhārī</s> (Destroyer); ta [is] <s>Bhairava</s>; tha [is] <s>Daṇḍī</s> (Staff-bearer); da [is] <s>Balibhuk</s> (Offering-eater); dha [is] <s>Ugrasūladhṛk</s> (Fierce Trident-holder); na [is] <s>Siṃhanādī</s> (Lion-roarer); pa [is] <s>Kapardī</s> (Matted-haired); pha [is] <s>Karālāgni</s> (Gaping Fire); ba [is] <s>Bhayaṃkara</s> (Fear-causer); bha [is] <s>Bahurūpī</s> (Many-formed); ma [is] <s>Mahākāla</s> (Great Time); ya [is] <s>Jīvātmā</s> (Individual Soul); ra [is] <s>Kṣatajokṣita</s> (Blood-sprinkled); la [is] <s>Balabhedī</s> (Strength-piercer); va [is] <s>Raktapaṭa</s> (Red-clothed); śa [is] <s>Caṇḍīśa</s> (Lord of Caṇḍī); ṣa [is] <s>Jvalanadhvaja</s> (Fire-bannered); sa [is] <s>Dhūmadhvaja</s> (Smoke-bannered); ha [is] <s>Vyomavaktra</s> (Sky-faced); kṣa [is] <s>Trailokyagrasanātmaka</s> (Devourer of the Three Worlds). (verse 2)

body.translated_text: <s>Vidyujjihvā</s> is black-faced, adorned with great time-beings. (verse 3)

body.text: viśabījaṃ śrutimukhaṃ dhruvaṃ hālāhalaṃ priye ca tat // 4
body.translated_text: The poison-seed, facing revelation, is certainly that <s>hālāhala</s> (cosmic poison), O beloved. (verse 4)

children.translated_text: <s>Caṇḍīśa</s> (śa) mounted on blood (ra), adorned by <s>Dhūmrabhairavī</s> (ī),
Joined with <s>nāda</s> and <s>bindu</s> — this seed is considered [that of] <s>Viṣṇupriyā</s> (Lakṣmī): śrīṃ. (verse 5)
Standing in blood (ra), sky-faced (ha), adorned by <s>Dhūmrabhairavī</s> (ī),
Joined with <s>nāda</s> and <s>bindu</s> — this is known as the primordial seed: hrīṃ. (verse 6)
<s>Krodhīśa</s> (ka) mounted on blood (ra), adorned by <s>Dhūmrabhairavī</s> (ī),
Joined with <s>nāda</s> and <s>bindu</s> — known as the dweller in the ancestral realm: krīṃ. (verse 7)
Joined with <s>Vidārī</s> (ū), sky-faced (ha), adorned by <s>Rudrarākiṇī</s> (aṃ),

children.text: kūrcaṃ kālaṃ krodhabījaṃ jānīhi vīravandite hūṃ // 8
children.translated_text: Know this as the <s>kūrca</s>, the dark, the wrath-seed, O one praised by heroes: hūṃ. (verse 8)
Taking <s>Ugrabhairavī</s> (ai) joined with <s>nāda</s> and <s>bindu</s>,

children.text: bhautikaṃ vāgbhavaṃ bījaṃ viddhi sārasvataṃ priye ai // 9
children.translated_text: Know this as the elemental, speech-origin seed, belonging to <s>Sarasvatī</s>, O beloved: aiṃ. (verse 9)

body.text: pralayāgnir mahājvālaḥ khyātaś cāstramanuḥ priye phaṭ // 10
body.translated_text: The fire of dissolution (pha) and the great flame (ṭa) — this is known as the weapon-<s>mantra</s>, O beloved: phaṭ. (verse 10)
<s>Krodhīśa</s> (ka) with blood (ra) and <s>Bhīmākṣī</s> (o) — this is the hook (<s>aṅkuśa</s>), possessing <s>nāda</s> and <s>bindu</s>: kroṃ. (verse 11)

body.text: dviṭhaḥ śiro vahnijāyā svāhā jvalanavallabhā svāhā // 12
body.translated_text: Two <s>Kapālīs</s> (ṭha ṭha) as the head, the wife of fire: <s>svāhā</s>, the beloved of the flame: <s>svāhā</s>. (verse 12)

children.translated_text: <s>Krodhīśa</s> (ka) with <s>Balabhedī</s> (la), with <s>Dhūmrabhairavī</s> (ī), <s>nāda</s> and <s>bindu</s>—

children.text: trimūrtir manmathaḥ kāmaḥ bījaṃ trailokyamohanam klīṃ // 13
children.translated_text: The three-formed, <s>Manmatha</s>, <s>Kāma</s> — this seed enchants the three worlds: klīṃ. (verse 13)
Sky-faced (ha) enhanced with <s>Kālarātrī</s> (u), the armor, joined with <s>bindu</s> and crescent—
This is called the armor seed, O beloved of <s>kulācāra</s> (clan practice), O pure one: huṃ. (verse 14)
Sky-faced (ha) mounted on blood (ra), with <s>Ḍākinī</s> (au), <s>nāda</s> and <s>bindu</s>—
This is proclaimed as the radiance <s>mantra</s>, the destroyer of great sins: hrauṃ. (verse 15)
Joined with <s>Dhūmrabhairavī</s> (ī), standing in blood (ra), the eater of offerings (da),
Joined with <s>nāda</s> and <s>bindu</s> — this is the supreme bell-seed: drīṃ. (verse 16)
Taking the many-formed one (bha), situated in the blood-sprinkled (ra),
Embraced by <s>Vidārī</s> (ū) — likewise the great <s>mantra</s> of special purpose: bhrūṃ. (verse 17)
Below the smoke-bannered one (sa), the fire of time (pha), with <s>Ūrdhvakeśī</s> (e), crescent and <s>bindu</s>—
The seed that causes the end of ages, revealed by <s>Bhairava</s>: spheṃ. (verse 18)
Supported by <s>Saṃhāriṇī</s>, and <s>Ūrdhvakeśinī</s> with <s>Kapardī</s> (pa),
Joined with <s>nāda</s> and <s>bindu</s> — this seed is known as the Vaitālika: pleṃ. (verse 19)
Taking <s>Krodhīśa</s> (ka) with <s>nāda</s> and <s>bindu</s>, situated in <s>Saṃhāriṇī</s>,

children.text: kampinībījam ity uktaṃ dviṭhenoktā manoharī klīṃ svāhā // 20
children.translated_text: This is called the trembling seed; with two <s>Kapālīs</s> (ṭha ṭha) is declared the enchantress: klīṃ svāhā. (verse 20)
Taking <s>Kapardī</s> (pa), situated in the blood-sprinkled (ra),
Joined with <s>Dhūmrabhairavī</s> (ī) — this is the crow [seed], possessing <s>nāda</s> and <s>bindu</s>: prīṃ. (verse 21)
Taking two <s>Kapālīs</s> (ṭha ṭha), adorned by <s>Mahākāla</s> (ma),

children.text: samāsanam iti proktaṃ caṇḍikāḍhyaṃ manoharam ṭhaṃ ṭhaṃ ṭhaḥ ṭhaḥ // 22
children.translated_text: This is called the seat (<s>samāsana</s>), enriched by <s>Caṇḍikā</s>, enchanting: ṭhaṃ ṭhaṃ ṭhaḥ ṭhaḥ. (verse 22)
The fire of dissolution (pha) situated, with the smoke-bannered one (sa) in the secret [place], possessing <s>bindu</s>,

children.text: saṃyukto dhūmrabhairavyā smṛtā phetkāriṇī priye sphīṃ // 23
children.translated_text: Joined with <s>Dhūmrabhairavī</s> (ī) — this is known as <s>Phetkāriṇī</s>, O beloved: sphīṃ. (verse 23)
Standing in blood (ra), sky-faced (ha), adorned with <s>bindu</s> and crescent,

children.text: khadyotam iti vikhyātaṃ grāsinī kālarātriyuk hruṃ // 24
children.translated_text: This is renowned as the firefly [seed], the devourer, joined with <s>Kālarātrī</s> (u): hruṃ. (verse 24)
Sky-faced (ha) standing in blood (ra), endowed with <s>nāda</s> and <s>bindu</s>,
Making <s>Vidārī</s> (ū) as ornament — this is the seed of <s>Vaivasvata</s> nature: hrūṃ. (verse 25)
Sky-faced (ha), smoke-bannered (sa), the elephant, of the nature of dissolution-fire (pha)—
With upward-flowing hair, mounted upon blood, conjoined with <s>bindu</s> and crescent moon. // 26

body.translated_text: The seed syllable of <s>Ānandabhairavī</s>, supremely bestowing silent bliss, is 'ha-sa-kha-phreṃ'. // 27

children.translated_text: In the letter 'a', the terrifying one, famed as <s>Vidyujjihvā</s> (Lightning-tongued),
In 'ā', <s>Tāmasī</s>, <s>Kālavajrī</s>, and <s>Kālabhairavī</s>. // 28
In 'i', the thundering fierce one is known as <s>Rudrabhairavī</s>,
In 'ī', the trident-bearing one is known as <s>Caṇḍogrā</s>, <s>Dhūmrabhairavī</s>. // 29
In 'u', the one called <s>Kālakūṭā</s>, the exceedingly fierce, beloved of <s>Caṇḍa</s>,
In 'ū', she is said to be <s>Vidārī</s>, <s>Tālajaṅghā</s>, <s>Kapālinī</s>. // 30

children.text: ṛkāre syān mahāraudrī jvālinī yoginīty api /
children.translated_text: In 'ṛ', she would be <s>Mahāraudrī</s>, <s>Jvālinī</s>, also called <s>Yoginī</s>,
In 'ṝ', she is said to be <s>Kālikā</s>, <s>Pitṛkālī</s>, the terrifying one. // 31
In 'ḷ', she would be <s>Saṃhāriṇī</s>, speaking fiercely with a thunder-like voice,
<s>Rudracaṇḍā</s>, <s>Kālarātri</s>, and in 'ḹ', <s>Karālinī</s>. // 32

children.text: ūrdhvakeśī ca cāmuṇḍā nādiny ekārake smṛtā /
children.translated_text: In 'e', she is remembered as <s>Ūrdhvakeśī</s>, <s>Cāmuṇḍā</s>, and <s>Nādinī</s>,
In 'ai', <s>Koṭarākṣī</s>, <s>Mālinī</s>, and <s>Unmattabhairavī</s>. // 33
In 'o', she is to be known as <s>Jvālinī</s>, <s>Bhīmākṣī</s>, and <s>Caṇḍamālinī</s>,
In 'au', <s>Ḍākinī</s>, <s>Siṃhanādinī</s>, and <s>Caṇḍabhairavī</s>. // 34
In 'aṃ', the one called <s>Akrūrā</s>, <s>Vidārī</s>, and <s>Rudrarākiṇī</s>,
In the remaining [visarga], <s>Kapālinī</s>, <s>Yāmyā</s>, <s>Caṇḍikā</s>; the two earrings. // 35

body.text: visargo nādaḥ sakalāḥ ṣaḍdaśoktāḥ svarā matāḥ // 36
body.translated_text: The <s>visarga</s>, <s>nāda</s>, and all components—sixteen vowels have been declared and recognized. // 36

children.translated_text: <s>Krodhīśa</s> (Lord of Wrath), <s>Vāraṇa</s>, <s>Caṇḍa</s>, <s>Śaṅka</s>, and <s>Unmattabhairava</s>,
<s>Jvālāmukha</s> (Flame-faced), <s>Raktadaṃṣṭra</s> (Blood-fanged), <s>Asitāṅga</s> (Dark-bodied), <s>Balayāmukha</s>. // 37
<s>Vidyunmukha</s> (Lightning-faced), <s>Mahājvali</s> (Greatly Blazing), <s>Kapālī</s> (Skull-bearer), <s>Bhīṣaṇa</s> (Terrifying), <s>Guru</s> (Weighty),
<s>Prahārī</s> (Striker), <s>Raurava</s> (Howling), <s>Daṇḍī</s> (Staff-bearer), <s>Balita</s>, and <s>Atyugraśūladhṛk</s> (Bearer of the Exceedingly Fierce Trident). // 38
<s>Siṃhanādī</s> (Lion-roarer), <s>Kapardī</s> (Matted-haired), <s>Pralayāgni</s> (Fire of Dissolution), <s>Bhayaṃkara</s> (Terror-causing),
<s>Bahurūpī</s> (Many-formed), <s>Mahākāla</s> (Great Time), <s>Sthirātmā</s> (Firm-souled), <s>Kṣatajokṣita</s> (Sprinkled with Blood). // 39
<s>Balabhedī</s> (Strength-splitter), <s>Raktapaṭa</s> (Red-clothed), <s>Caṇḍīśa</s> (Lord of the Fierce One), <s>Jvalanadhvaja</s> (Fire-bannered),
<s>Dhūmadhvaja</s> (Smoke-bannered), <s>Vyomavaktra</s> (Sky-faced), <s>Trailokyagrasanātmaka</s> (Whose Nature is Devouring the Three Worlds). // 40

body.translated_text: In the <s>nyāsa</s> (ritual placement) upon the eyes, ears, mouth, nose, and heart, the ten vowels are placed. // 41

children.translated_text: <s>Dhvajinī</s> and <s>Dhūmrabhairavī</s> are remembered in the manifestation of the two eyes,
The root syllable is declared upon the chest; the <s>hṛdaya</s> (heart mantra) consists of the vowel-powers. // 42
At the beginning, middle, and end, in the absence of the preceding, each succeeding one follows,
Throat-and-mouth, adorned by <s>Kālavaktra</s> (Time-faced) and <s>Mahākāla</s> (Great Time),
Beginning with that, the five rays and creation, preservation, dissolution, and poison. // 43
<s>Caṇḍīśa</s>, stationed in fire, accompanied by <s>Śūlinī</s> (trident-bearer), possessing the moon-<s>bindu</s>,

children.text: etad viṣṇupriyābījaṃ yan mānyaṃ jagataḥ priyam // 44
children.translated_text: This is the seed syllable of <s>Viṣṇupriyā</s> (Beloved of Viṣṇu), which is venerable and dear to the world. // 44
Stationed upon blood, sky-faced, adorned with the <s>bindu</s> of <s>Caṇḍogrā</s>,

children.text: adrijā raudrī bhūteśī bījam prāthamikaṃ priyam // 45
children.translated_text: The Mountain-born, <s>Raudrī</s>, <s>Bhūteśī</s> (Mistress of Beings)—this is the primary and beloved seed syllable. // 45
<s>Krodhīśa</s> (Lord of Wrath), stationed in blood, adorned by <s>Dhūmrabhairavī</s>,
Conjoined with double <s>bindu</s>, this seed syllable is known for melting and moistening. // 46
Sky-faced, conjoined with <s>bindu</s>, adorned by <s>Tālajaṅghā</s>,
<s>Kūrcakāla</s>, <s>Mahākāla</s> (Great Time)—this is the wrath seed syllable, stainless. // 47
Adorned by <s>Unmattabhairavī</s> and <s>Rudraḍākinī</s>,
Ornamented with <s>nāda</s>, this is the <s>Vāgbhava</s> (Speech-origin) seed syllable, which increases wisdom. // 48

body.text: phaḍ ity astraṃ prasiddhaṃ syāj phaṭ // 49
body.translated_text: 'Phaḍ' is the well-known weapon mantra; 'Phaṭ'. // 49
Blazing fire, the all-pervading goad; 'Kror'. // 50
The head mantra is 'Svāhā,' doubled; the wife of fire, beloved of the flame. // 51
The two right knees, with the moon; the divine face, <s>Vahnisundarī</s> (Beauty of Fire)—'Svāhā'. // 52

body.text: indrāsanagato brahmā trimūrtīnduś ca manmathaḥ klīṃ // 53
body.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> seated on <s>Indra's</s> throne, the three-formed moon, and <s>Manmatha</s> (God of Love)—'Klīṃ'. // 53

children.translated_text: <s>Garjinī</s> and <s>Dhūmrabhairavī</s> are the right and left breasts,
Sky-faced, enriched by <s>Kālavaktra</s>, conjoined with armor-<s>bindu</s> and moon—'Huṃ'. // 54
The void, mounted upon blood, adorned by <s>Caṇḍabhairavī</s>,
Conjoined with <s>nāda</s> and <s>bindu</s> at the crown—the luminous mantra is declared as 'Hrauṃ'. // 55
The supreme treasury of mantras, taught by the Primordial Lord,

children.text: yad arthibhyaḥ purā guptaṃ tan mayādya prakāśitam // 56
children.translated_text: That which was formerly kept secret from seekers is now revealed by me. // 56
This is the elucidation of the mantra treasury of the <s>Yakṣaḍāmaratantra</s>,

children.text: krodhīśena tu yat proktaṃ bhairavāya mahātmane // 57
children.translated_text: Which was spoken by <s>Krodhīśa</s> (Lord of Wrath) to the great-souled <s>Bhairava</s>. // 57
<s>Vidyuccaṇḍā</s>, <s>Āśinī</s>, <s>Gaurī</s>, <s>Krośinī</s>, <s>Nāginī</s>, <s>Jayā</s>,

children.text: kiṃnarī yoginī yakṣī bhūtinī pretinī narī // 58
children.translated_text: <s>Kiṃnarī</s>, <s>Yoginī</s>, <s>Yakṣī</s>, <s>Bhūtinī</s>, <s>Pretinī</s>, <s>Narī</s>, // 58

children.text: grāsinī trāsinī caṇḍī kalety evaṃ prakīrtitā /
children.translated_text: <s>Grāsinī</s>, <s>Trāsinī</s>, <s>Caṇḍī</s>, <s>Kalā</s>—thus they are proclaimed,
In the <s>Kālabhairava</s> tantra, among all the immortal ones, and among the earth-plough goddesses. // 59
<s>Subhagā</s>, <s>Sumukhī</s>, <s>Caṇḍī</s>, <s>Pārvatī</s>, <s>Suratapriyā</s>,

children.text: urvaśī caindriṇī līlā kaṅkālī mekhalā śacī // 60
children.translated_text: <s>Urvaśī</s>, <s>Caindriṇī</s>, <s>Līlā</s>, <s>Kaṅkālī</s>, <s>Mekhalā</s>, <s>Śacī</s>, // 60

children.text: māninī haṃsinī caulā kalanā bhūminīti ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Māninī</s>, <s>Haṃsinī</s>, <s>Caulā</s>, <s>Kalanā</s>, and <s>Bhūminī</s>.
The powers of the first lords, as declared by the primordial deity (<s>Ādideva</s>).

children.text: vibhramo bāhulo daṇḍī bhairavo naṭakaḥ śukaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Vibhrama</s>, <s>Bāhula</s>, <s>Daṇḍī</s>, <s>Bhairava</s>, <s>Naṭaka</s>, <s>Śuka</s>,

children.text: vṛkodaro jaṭo bhīṣmaḥ kṣobhakaḥ khecaro naṭaḥ // 62
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛkodara</s>, <s>Jaṭa</s>, <s>Bhīṣma</s>, <s>Kṣobhaka</s>, <s>Khecara</s>, <s>Naṭa</s>.

children.text: niśācarā dhvajī bhīmo vicitraḥ kauśiko yamaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Niśācara</s>, <s>Dhvajī</s>, <s>Bhīma</s>, <s>Vicitra</s>, <s>Kauśika</s>, <s>Yama</s>,
<s>Liṅgī</s>, <s>Vatsādhika</s>, <s>Bhṛṅgī</s>, <s>Maṇibhadra</s>, <s>Ghaṭotkaca</s>.

children.text: mahānandī śuko daṇḍī sugrīvaḥ kalaho bhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Mahānandī</s>, <s>Śuka</s>, <s>Daṇḍī</s>, <s>Sugrīva</s>, <s>Kalaha</s>, <s>Bhava</s>,

children.text: daṇḍī bhāṣāntako 'jeśo gargo haṃsaḥ pakṣaiścaro halī // 64
children.translated_text: <s>Daṇḍī</s>, <s>Bhāṣāntaka</s>, <s>Ajeśa</s>, <s>Garga</s>, <s>Haṃsa</s>, <s>Pakṣaiścara</s>, <s>Halī</s>.
The seed syllable (<s>bīja</s>) of <s>Caṇḍī</s> is thus known, [composed] of <s>Vidyut</s>, <s>Nāga</s>, <s>Aṅganā</s>, and <s>Aṃśuka</s>;

children.text: aurasādhike 'ṃśukādyā ca dhūminy asau kiṃnaraḥ smṛtaḥ // 65
children.translated_text: with <s>Aurasa</s>, <s>Adhika</s>, <s>Aṃśuka</s> and the rest, and <s>Dhūminī</s> — this is known as <s>Kiṃnara</s>.

body.translated_text: <s>Haṃsa</s> adorned by <s>Urvaśī</s>, <s>Haṃsa</s> uplifted with the moon on the head — HŪṂ.

body.text: vidyuccaṇḍā ca haṃsī ca ketur nāginyalaṃkṛtā ha // 67
body.translated_text: <s>Vidyut</s>, <s>Caṇḍā</s>, and <s>Haṃsī</s>, and <s>Ketu</s> adorned by <s>Nāginī</s> — HA.

body.text: ḍiṇḍibhena saraktena kāminī bindubhiḥ śaśī śrīṃ // 68
body.translated_text: By <s>Ḍiṇḍibha</s> with redness, <s>Kāminī</s>, with <s>bindus</s> (dots), the moon — ŚRĪṂ.
Adorned with <s>Haṃsa</s>, <s>Grīva</s>, <s>Pārvatī</s>, <s>Kapardī</s>, the moon and so forth — HRĪṂ.
<s>Vigraha</s>, <s>Kalaha</s>, <s>Kāminī</s>, the moon and so forth — the life-stealing one — KRĪṂ.
<s>Vibhrama</s> and red <s>Pārvatī</s> with <s>Svāhā</s> — this is known as <s>Ulkāmukhī</s>.
Known as <s>Jvālaṃdharī</s>, with <s>bindu</s>, <s>indu</s> (moon), <s>kalā</s> (digit), and <s>Naṭī</s>.

body.text: haṃsaḥ sugrīvaḥ caṇḍādyaiḥ khadyotaiḥ parikīrtitā hraṃ // 73
body.translated_text: <s>Haṃsa</s>, <s>Sugrīva</s>, with <s>Caṇḍā</s> and others, proclaimed by fireflies (<s>khadyota</s>) — HRAṂ.
That one whose body is embraced by <s>Śyāmā</s>, the firefly, is declared as light — HRAUṂ.

body.text: yamaḥ sugrīvaḥ kāminīndrendvādyaiḥ kiṃnarīti ca hruṃ // 75
body.translated_text: <s>Yama</s>, <s>Sugrīva</s>, with <s>Kāminī</s>, <s>Indra</s>, the moon and so forth — this is called <s>Kiṃnarī</s>, HRUṂ.

body.text: sugrīvo 'pi yamaś caṇḍo nīlādyair vāṇa īritaḥ drāṃ // 76
body.translated_text: <s>Sugrīva</s> also, <s>Yama</s>, <s>Caṇḍa</s>, with <s>Nīlā</s> and others — this is called the arrow (<s>vāṇa</s>), DRĀṂ.
<s>Yama</s>, <s>Sugrīva</s>, <s>bindu</s>, the moon, <s>japa</s> and so forth — the flesh-eater (<s>piśitāśana</s>), DRUṂ.

children.translated_text: The renouncer, established in <s>Maṇibhadra</s>, adorned with <s>Pretinī</s>, the moon and so forth,
the seed syllable causing the end of the age — revealed by <s>Bhairava</s>, SPHREṂ.
Of <s>Bhṛṅgī</s>, joined with a girdle (<s>mekhalā</s>), adorned with <s>Pretinī</s>, the moon and so forth —

children.text: bījaṃ vaitālikaṃ proktaṃ dviṭhenoktā manoharī pleṃ svāhā // 79
children.translated_text: the <s>Vaitālika</s> seed syllable is declared, and <s>Manoharī</s> is declared with two <s>ṭhas</s>, PLEṂ SVĀHĀ.
<s>Vibhrama</s>, <s>Dhūminī</s>, <s>Vidyut</s>, <s>Caṇḍikā</s> and the rest — this is <s>Kākinī</s>;

children.text: dhvāṅkṣabījam iti khyātaṃ sarvatantreṣu gopitaṃ prīṃ // 80
children.translated_text: the crow (<s>dhvāṅkṣa</s>) seed syllable is thus known, concealed in all <s>tantras</s>, PRĪṂ.

body.text: naṭadvayena dhūminyā ūrdhvakeśyā hy alaṃkṛtaṃ phreṃ // 81
body.translated_text: Adorned with two <s>Naṭas</s>, <s>Dhūminī</s>, and <s>Ūrdhvakeśī</s> — PHREṂ.
<s>Naṭa</s> joined with <s>Dhavāna</s>, with <s>Naṭī</s> having sharp breasts — ṬAṂṬHAṂ.

children.translated_text: Embraced by <s>Pārvatī</s>, established in <s>Maṇibhadra</s>, O beloved of the <s>yoginīs</s>,
[this is] known as <s>Phetkāriṇī</s>, adorned with <s>Vidyut</s> and <s>Caṇḍa</s>, SPHĪṂ.
<s>Sugrīva</s>, dissolution of bones, in the ear, with pleasing and complete sight;

children.text: vikalāyāḥ svabhāve ca syād gaurīti ca pārvatī // 84
children.translated_text: in the nature of the incomplete — this would be <s>Gaurī</s> and also <s>Pārvatī</s>.
The root syllable (<s>mūlārṇa</s>) is declared as the month; the heart [syllable] and the vowel powers —
they are to be understood successively in creation, sustenance, and dissolution.
Declared by the primordial deity, in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, in the <s>Kali</s> age,
this treasury of <s>mantras</s> (<s>mantrakośa</s>) from the <s>Bhūta</s>, <s>Yakṣa</s>, and <s>Ḍāmara</s> tantras,

body.translated_text: [is] for the benefit of mortals, rare in the three worlds.
